newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain's Alba expansion to come on stream in Jan.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain's Alba expansion to come on stream in Jan.

text.p: An Aluminium Bahrain BSC (Alba) expansion project has been completed ahead of schedule and 36,500 tonnes a year of new capacity will come on stream in January, Alba's chief executive Gudvin Tofte said on Monday.
"Alba's expansion has already been completed and we will be producing at full capacity from January 1," Tofte told Reuters.
The $130 million expansion, originally scheduled for completion in May 1997, will add 36,500 tonnes a year to the smelter's current annual production capacity of 460,000 tonnes.

Built in 1971 as part of plans to diversify Bahrain's economy, Alba is now the largest aluminium producer in the Middle East. It is 77 percent owned by the Bahrain government, while Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund owns 20 percent and German group Breton Investments holds the rest.

Alba Chairman Sheikh Isa bin Ali al-Khalifa, who is also oil and industry minister, has said Alba's production was expected to hit a record in 1996. Last year Alba produced 450,700 tonnes, up from 449,400 tonnes in 1994.

Tofte said Alba had used diplomatic channels to urge the European Union to lift its six percent aluminium import tariff, imposed to offset dollar fluctuations and the effect of cheap imports from the Middle East Gulf.
"We are supporting the removal of the six percent tariff... We have taken necessary steps through various channels including diplomatic," Tofte said.

In November, Tofte told Alba's newsletter that raw material now represents between 50 and 60 percent of the smelter's operating costs, "which was relatively higher than in the past". He gave no figures.
"In future, we should be looking into integration with regard to raw materials as well as semi-manufactures abroad," he told Reuters.
Alba imports alumina mainly from Australia and petroleum coke from the United States.
